cards.name: The Fool
cards.upright_meaning: The Fool represents new beginnings, having faith in the future, being inexperienced, not knowing what to expect, having beginner's luck, improvisation, and believing in the universe. You are at the start of a new journey, full of optimism and excitement. The world is your oyster and anything is possible. Take that leap of faith even if you don't feel 100% ready.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Fool reversed suggests recklessness, risk-taking, and poor judgment. You may be rushing into something without thinking it through. There is a sense of naivety that borders on foolishness. You may be taking unnecessary risks or failing to plan for the future. Consider whether you are being too impulsive.
cards.symbolism: The Fool carries a small bag on a stick representing untapped potential and experiences. The white sun behind him symbolizes divine wisdom and protection. The mountains in the background represent future challenges. The small dog at his heels represents loyalty and the natural world. He stands at the edge of a cliff, about to step off into the unknown.

cards.name: The Magician
cards.upright_meaning: The Magician represents your ability to communicate clearly, to 'sell' yourself or your ideas, and to be resourceful. You have all the tools and resources available to manifest your desires. This is a time of inspired action, creation, and manifestation. You have the power to turn your dreams into reality through focused willpower and skill.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Magician reversed warns of manipulation, poor planning, and untapped talents. You may be using your skills for deception or manipulation, or you may be failing to make use of the gifts you have. There is potential that is not being expressed. Watch out for tricksters or con artists in your life.
cards.symbolism: The Magician stands before a table holding all four suit symbols: a cup, pentacle, sword, and wand. He points one hand to the sky and one to the earth, channeling divine energy into the material world. The infinity symbol above his head represents unlimited potential. The red roses and white lilies represent passion and purity.

cards.name: The High Priestess
cards.upright_meaning: The High Priestess represents your intuition, higher powers, and the subconscious mind. She sits between the conscious and subconscious, inviting you to trust your inner voice. Now is a time to look inward and listen to your gut feelings. Something is hidden and not yet ready to be revealed. Meditate and trust what cannot be seen.
cards.reversed_meaning: The High Priestess reversed suggests secrets, hidden agendas, and a disconnect from intuition. You may be ignoring your inner voice, or information is being kept from you. You may be too focused on the external world and neglecting your spiritual life. Reconnect with your intuition and the power of your subconscious mind.
cards.symbolism: She sits between two pillars, B and J (Boaz and Jachin from Solomon's Temple), representing duality. The veil behind her is decorated with pomegranates, symbolizing fertility and abundance. She holds a scroll labeled TORA, representing hidden knowledge. The crescent moon at her feet represents the cycles of nature and feminine energy.

cards.name: The Empress
cards.upright_meaning: The Empress represents the divine feminine and the abundance of Mother Earth. She is a sign of fertility, creativity, and nurturing. This card encourages you to connect with nature, embrace your senses, and nurture yourself and others. A time of creativity and abundance is at hand. You may be pregnant with new ideas or a literal child.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Empress reversed can indicate creative blocks, dependence on others, or smothering. You may be struggling to feel creative or fertile. There could be issues around co-dependency or an over-reliance on others for your sense of worth. It can also suggest neglecting self-care or issues with your relationship to your body or to nature.
cards.symbolism: The Empress sits on a cushioned throne in a lush forest. She wears a crown of twelve stars representing the twelve months and zodiac signs. Her robe is decorated with pomegranates. She holds a scepter representing her power. A shield with the Venus symbol rests nearby. Wheat grows at her feet, symbolizing abundance and harvest.

cards.name: The Emperor
cards.upright_meaning: The Emperor represents authority, structure, and the archetypal father figure. He brings stability through rules, discipline, and order. This card encourages you to create solid foundations and take a systematic, logical approach to your goals. You may need to be more assertive and take charge. A powerful, authoritative figure may be influential in your life.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Emperor reversed suggests tyranny, rigidity, and an abuse of power. Authority figures may be dominating or controlling. You may be struggling with someone who is overly rigid or inflexible. Alternatively, you may be giving away your personal power or struggling to assert yourself. There is a need to find balance between control and flexibility.
cards.symbolism: The Emperor sits on a stone throne adorned with ram heads, representing Aries. He holds an ankh scepter in his right hand (life) and an orb in his left (dominion). He wears armor beneath his robe, suggesting readiness for battle. The barren mountains behind him represent his authority over the material world.

cards.name: The Hierophant
cards.upright_meaning: The Hierophant represents traditional institutions, spiritual authority, and conformity to established norms. He is a bridge between the sacred and the mundane. You may be seeking conventional wisdom, spiritual guidance from an established tradition, or mentorship. It can also represent a need to follow the rules and social conventions of a group or institution.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Hierophant reversed suggests challenging tradition, breaking rules, and seeking personal freedom from conventional norms. You may feel constrained by rigid structures or dogma. This is a time to question authority and think for yourself. It can also indicate unconventional relationships or alternative spiritual paths.
cards.symbolism: The Hierophant sits between two pillars and raises his hand in a blessing gesture. Two followers kneel before him. He wears three robes representing the three worlds, and a three-tiered crown. He holds a triple cross scepter. The crossed keys at his feet represent the balance between the conscious and subconscious mind.

cards.name: The Lovers
cards.upright_meaning: The Lovers represents love, harmony, and alignment of values. It often points to an important choice or crossroads, not necessarily romantic. You are being called to make a decision that aligns with your core values. In relationships, this card speaks to deep connection and mutual respect. This is about choosing what you truly value and staying true to your authentic self.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Lovers reversed warns of disharmony, imbalance, and misalignment of values. You may be avoiding a difficult decision or making choices that don't align with your values. In relationships, there may be conflict, infidelity, or a loss of shared values. You may be overly dependent on another person or struggling with self-love.
cards.symbolism: A man and woman stand naked beneath an angel, representing the conscious and subconscious mind under divine guidance. The woman stands before the Tree of Knowledge (with a serpent), representing temptation. The man stands before the Tree of Life. The sun-drenched mountain between them represents challenges. The angel above blesses their union.

cards.name: The Chariot
cards.upright_meaning: The Chariot represents willpower, determination, and the drive to succeed against all odds. You are in control and moving forward with confidence and purpose. Victory is within reach if you maintain focus and discipline. This card encourages you to assert yourself and push through obstacles. Success comes through maintaining control of opposing forces.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Chariot reversed suggests lack of direction, aggression, and feeling out of control. You may be forcing outcomes that are not meant to be, or you may feel like your life is pulling you in too many different directions. There is a need to regain control and focus your energy. Watch for recklessness or aggression.
cards.symbolism: The charioteer stands in a vehicle with a canopy of stars, pulled by two sphinxes — one black and one white — representing opposing forces. He holds a wand and wears armor with crescent moons, representing the need to bring emotions under control. The city behind him is left behind as he moves forward into victory.

cards.name: Strength
cards.upright_meaning: Strength represents inner strength, compassion, and the ability to influence through love rather than force. You have what it takes to overcome your challenges. This card encourages patience, quiet confidence, and taming your instincts with kindness. True strength is not about physical power but about emotional mastery and spiritual courage.
cards.reversed_meaning: Strength reversed warns of inner doubt, weakness, and lack of confidence. You may be struggling to find the inner resources you need to handle a difficult situation. There could be issues with anger, self-discipline, or an inability to control your instincts. Reconnect with your inner power and trust your abilities.
cards.symbolism: A woman gently holds open the jaws of a lion. She wears a white robe representing purity and an infinity symbol crowns her head. Flowers adorn both her and the lion, representing the taming of raw nature through gentleness. The mountains in the distance represent endurance.

cards.name: The Hermit
cards.upright_meaning: The Hermit represents a period of introspection and withdrawal from the external world to focus on your inner life. You are searching for deeper meaning and truth. This is a time for soul-searching, meditation, and seeking wisdom from within. The Hermit may also represent a mentor or wise guide who illuminates your path with their light.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Hermit reversed suggests isolation, loneliness, and withdrawal. You may be retreating too far from the world or refusing the wisdom of others. Alternatively, it can indicate that a period of necessary solitude is coming to an end and it is time to rejoin the world. Watch for antisocial behavior or paranoia.
cards.symbolism: An old man stands on a snowy mountain peak, carrying a lantern with a six-pointed star and a long staff. The star represents the light of wisdom. The mountain represents achievement and the cold heights of wisdom. His grey cloak represents invisibility. He looks down, lighting the way for others who follow his path.

cards.name: Wheel of Fortune
cards.upright_meaning: The Wheel of Fortune represents the cyclical nature of life, fate, and unexpected change. This is a turning point — fortune may be smiling on you. What goes around comes around. This card invites you to embrace change and trust in the natural flow of the universe. Opportunities are presenting themselves; be ready to take advantage of them.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Wheel of Fortune reversed suggests bad luck, resistance to change, and breaking cycles. Negative patterns may be repeating in your life. You may be resisting the inevitable changes the universe is bringing. There is a sense that you are not in control of your circumstances. Look for ways to regain agency and break negative cycles.
cards.symbolism: A great wheel sits in the sky surrounded by four winged creatures in the corners: an angel (Aquarius), eagle (Scorpio), lion (Leo), and bull (Taurus). A sphinx sits atop the wheel, a serpent descends on the left, and Anubis rises on the right. The wheel bears alchemical symbols and Hebrew letters spelling TARO (or ROTA, the wheel).

cards.name: Justice
cards.upright_meaning: Justice represents fairness, truth, and the law of cause and effect. Your actions have consequences and you will be held accountable. This card encourages you to make decisions with integrity and ensure that your choices are fair and just. A legal matter may be coming to a favorable resolution. Truth will prevail.
cards.reversed_meaning: Justice reversed warns of unfairness, dishonesty, and an avoidance of accountability. A legal matter may not go in your favor. Someone may be acting unjustly or you may be refusing to take responsibility for your actions. There is a need to examine your own sense of fairness and integrity.
cards.symbolism: A crowned figure sits between two pillars, holding scales in one hand and a sword in the other. The scales represent impartiality and balance. The double-edged sword represents the logical, decisive mind. The square on her crown represents ordered thought. A purple veil hangs behind her, representing compassion.

cards.name: The Hanged Man
cards.upright_meaning: The Hanged Man represents a voluntary pause, surrender, and seeing things from a new perspective. You may feel stuck or in limbo, but this is actually a time of spiritual growth. By letting go of control and surrendering to the universe, you gain enlightenment. Sometimes you must sacrifice something to gain greater wisdom.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Hanged Man reversed suggests resistance to change, stalling, and an inability to let go. You may be delaying the inevitable or refusing to make a necessary sacrifice. You may be martyring yourself unnecessarily. It is time to release what no longer serves you and move forward.
cards.symbolism: A figure hangs upside down from one foot from a T-shaped cross made of living wood. His face is serene and a halo of light surrounds his head, indicating enlightenment. His free leg is crossed behind the hanging one, forming an inverted figure four. His hands are bound behind his back. The living tree suggests life even in sacrifice.

cards.name: Death
cards.upright_meaning: Death rarely represents physical death. Instead, it signifies endings, transformation, and the closing of one chapter so another can begin. Something in your life is coming to an end, making way for something new. This transition may be difficult but is necessary for your growth. Embrace change rather than resisting it.
cards.reversed_meaning: Death reversed suggests resistance to change, stagnation, and an inability to move on. You may be clinging to the past or refusing to let something end that has run its course. This resistance is preventing your growth and forward movement. It is time to accept the ending and allow transformation to occur.
cards.symbolism: A skeleton in black armor rides a white horse. Before him lie the dead and dying: a king, a bishop, a maiden, and a child. A black flag bears a white rose — a symbol of purity and immortality. In the background, the sun sets between two towers, symbolizing the end of one day and the beginning of another.

cards.name: Temperance
cards.upright_meaning: Temperance represents balance, moderation, and a sense of higher purpose. You are finding middle ground and blending opposite forces harmoniously. This is a time of patience, calm, and healing. Everything is working together in perfect proportion. You are being guided by a higher power toward your true path.
cards.reversed_meaning: Temperance reversed suggests imbalance, excess, and lack of moderation. You may be overindulging in something or failing to find the middle ground. There is a sense of impatience and conflict. Things are not flowing smoothly. It is time to step back and find balance before moving forward.
cards.symbolism: An angel with great wings stands with one foot in water and one on land, representing the balance of the material and emotional worlds. The angel pours water between two cups, representing the flow and alchemy of life. A triangle within a square on the angel's robe represents the earthly being within the higher spiritual laws. A path leads to a mountain crown.

cards.name: The Devil
cards.upright_meaning: The Devil represents bondage, addiction, and the shadow side of our nature. You may feel trapped by material concerns, unhealthy relationships, or destructive patterns. However, the chains are loose — you have the power to free yourself. This card invites you to examine what is keeping you in bondage and to confront your shadow self.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Devil reversed represents breaking free from bondage, releasing limiting beliefs, and reclaiming power. You are becoming aware of the chains that bind you and taking steps to free yourself. It can also indicate a period of detox or recovery, or a realization that what you thought was holding you back was actually an illusion.
cards.symbolism: A horned, winged devil sits on a pedestal. Below him, a man and woman are chained to his throne, but the chains are loose enough to be removed easily. The couple has grown horns and tails, showing the corrupting influence of materialism. An inverted pentagram above the devil's head represents the material overriding the spiritual.

cards.name: The Tower
cards.upright_meaning: The Tower represents sudden, disruptive change that shatters illusions and false foundations. What is built on shaky ground will crumble. Though this is often experienced as traumatic, it is ultimately liberating. The old must be destroyed to make way for something more authentic and true. This is a necessary breakthrough, not just a breakdown.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Tower reversed suggests narrowly avoiding disaster, resisting necessary change, or a delayed crisis. You may be avoiding a necessary shake-up out of fear. The upheaval may be more internal than external. There is still turbulence, but you have more control. Consider making proactive changes before the universe forces them.
cards.symbolism: A tall tower is struck by lightning and catches fire. Two figures fall from the tower headfirst. The crown at the top has been blown off, representing the overthrow of ego and false beliefs. The lightning represents divine revelation and sudden truth. The flames are actually the 22 Yods — divine blessings — raining down.

cards.name: The Star
cards.upright_meaning: The Star represents hope, renewal, and a sense of divine guidance after hardship. This is a time of healing and restoration. You are being replenished spiritually and emotionally. Have faith in the universe and in your own potential. Your dreams are valid and the universe is supporting you. Peace and calm follow the storm.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Star reversed suggests despair, hopelessness, and a loss of faith. You may be feeling disconnected from your higher purpose or unable to see the light at the end of the tunnel. Reconnect with what gives you hope. It can also indicate that you are placing unrealistic expectations on yourself or others.
cards.symbolism: A naked woman kneels at the edge of a pool of water. She pours water from two jugs — one into the water, one onto the land — representing the replenishment of both the subconscious and conscious mind. Above her shines one large eight-pointed star surrounded by seven smaller ones. A bird perches in a tree in the background.

cards.name: The Moon
cards.upright_meaning: The Moon represents illusion, fear, and the deep unconscious. Things are not as they seem. You may be experiencing confusion, anxiety, or unsettling dreams. Your subconscious is communicating something important. Trust your intuition rather than what appears on the surface. Navigate this uncertain time by listening to your inner wisdom.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Moon reversed suggests that confusion is lifting and illusions are dissolving. Secrets may be revealed. You are beginning to see through deception or emerging from a period of confusion and self-deception. It can also indicate repressed anxiety, fear, or unresolved emotional issues that need to be addressed.
cards.symbolism: A full moon shines between two towers on either side of a winding path that leads into the mountains. A crayfish emerges from a pool, representing the subconscious rising. A dog and wolf howl at the moon, representing the tame and wild aspects of our minds. Fifteen Yods (divine light) fall from the moon.

cards.name: The Sun
cards.upright_meaning: The Sun is one of the most positive cards in the tarot. It represents success, vitality, joy, and abundance. Life is good and you are able to see it clearly. Your efforts are paying off. This is a time of great optimism and confidence. Children, creativity, and playfulness are highlighted. Everything is illuminated and visible.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Sun reversed suggests temporary setbacks to happiness, clouded optimism, or an inability to see the positive. You may be feeling low on energy or struggling to find joy. However, the Sun reversed still holds the energy of the upright card — the cloud will pass. You may be setting unrealistic expectations or being overly optimistic.
cards.symbolism: A large, radiant sun shines in the sky. Below it, a naked child sits on a white horse, holding a red banner. Four sunflowers grow in a walled garden behind the child. The child represents the joy and purity of childhood. The white horse represents purity and nobility. The sunflowers represent life and the fertility of the earth.

cards.name: Judgement
cards.upright_meaning: Judgement represents a moment of reckoning, awakening, and profound transformation. You are being called to rise up and embrace your higher calling. This is a time of reflection, evaluation, and spiritual renewal. Past actions are being assessed. Forgive yourself and others and answer the call to a higher purpose. Rebirth is at hand.
cards.reversed_meaning: Judgement reversed suggests self-doubt, refusal of self-examination, and an inability to heed the call to action. You may be too hard on yourself or avoiding a necessary reckoning. There could be guilt, shame, or a fear of judgment preventing your growth. It is time for honest self-evaluation and forgiveness.
cards.symbolism: The archangel Gabriel blows a trumpet from which hangs a banner with a red cross. Below, men and women of all ages rise from their graves with arms outstretched, answering the call. Grey mountains tower in the background, representing insurmountable obstacles that are overcome by this divine call.

cards.name: The World
cards.upright_meaning: The World represents successful completion, wholeness, and the attainment of your goals. A major life chapter is closing and you have gained everything you set out to gain. You have reached a point of integration where all parts of yourself work together harmoniously. Celebrate your achievements and prepare for a new cycle to begin.
cards.reversed_meaning: The World reversed suggests incompletion, stagnation, and failure to reach closure. You may be so close to completing something but find it dragging on. There are loose ends that need tying up. You may be lacking commitment or taking shortcuts. It is time to push through to completion before beginning the next chapter.
cards.symbolism: A dancing figure wrapped in a purple cloth holds two wands and is encircled by a laurel wreath. In the four corners are the same four fixed signs as the Wheel of Fortune: a man (Aquarius), eagle (Scorpio), lion (Leo), and bull (Taurus), representing the four elements and the mastery of the material world.

cards.name: Ace of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Ace of Wands represents a spark of inspiration and the birth of a new creative project or venture. This is a time of tremendous potential and enthusiasm. You are being called to take action on a new idea. Seize this opportunity with passion and confidence. The universe is offering you a powerful burst of creative energy.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Ace of Wands reversed suggests delays, blocked creativity, and lack of direction. A new project may be stalling or failing to get off the ground. You may be experiencing creative blocks or a lack of motivation. The energy is there but it is not being channeled effectively. Revisit your plans and reignite your passion.
cards.symbolism: A hand emerges from a cloud holding a wooden wand with leaves sprouting from it, symbolizing growth and potential. A castle sits in the background on a hill. The landscape is lush and green, representing fertility and abundance.

cards.name: Two of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Two of Wands represents planning for the future and making decisions about the direction of your life. You have achieved initial success and are now looking to expand your horizons. The world is at your feet. This is a time of bold vision and strategic planning. Consider all your options before committing to a path.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Two of Wands reversed suggests poor planning, fear of the unknown, and a lack of vision. You may be too cautious or failing to plan properly for the future. There is a sense of stagnation and an unwillingness to take risks. You may also be struggling with a fear of change or an inability to make decisions.
cards.symbolism: A man stands on a battlement holding a small globe, gazing at the sea. Two wands flank him — one he holds, one is attached to the wall. He is dressed in fine clothes, suggesting established success. The globe represents the world he wishes to conquer. He looks outward toward unexplored horizons.

cards.name: Three of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Three of Wands represents expansion, foresight, and the first steps of a long journey. Your plans are in motion and ships are coming in — literally or figuratively. This is a time of waiting for results while already looking ahead to the next phase. Expand your horizons; opportunities may come from distant places.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Three of Wands reversed suggests delays in plans, obstacles, and a lack of foresight. Things may not be coming together as expected. Plans may be falling through or facing unexpected setbacks. You may be struggling with impatience or a tendency to look too far ahead without attending to the present.
cards.symbolism: A figure stands with his back turned, looking out over a vast sea with three wands planted firmly in the ground around him. Ships sail in the distance, representing ventures already underway. The mountains in the background represent the obstacles already overcome.

cards.name: Four of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Four of Wands represents celebration, harmony, and a joyful homecoming. This is a time of happiness and achievement worth celebrating. There is a sense of community, togetherness, and the joy of milestones reached. This card often appears around weddings, graduations, reunions, and other celebratory events. Enjoy this moment of peace and stability.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Four of Wands reversed suggests a delay in celebration, conflict at home, or a lack of harmony in your close relationships. A celebration or homecoming may be postponed or disrupted. There may be tension within your family or community. Alternatively, it can indicate a private celebration or a personal achievement that has not yet been shared.
cards.symbolism: Four wands are planted in the ground forming a canopy decorated with garlands of flowers and fruit. Two figures dance joyfully in the foreground. In the background, a crowd of people celebrate before a grand castle. The entire scene radiates joy, abundance, and festivity.

cards.name: Five of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Five of Wands represents conflict, competition, and tension arising from differences of opinion. You may be in the thick of a competitive environment or dealing with conflict and disagreement. This can be productive tension that leads to growth and better solutions, or it can be disruptive chaos. Channel the energy into healthy competition.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Five of Wands reversed suggests an avoidance of conflict, inner conflict, or the end of a dispute. You may be suppressing aggression or avoiding necessary confrontation. Conflict may be coming to an end. Alternatively, there could be hidden competition or conflict that is not being addressed openly.
cards.symbolism: Five young men each hold a wand and appear to be fighting or sparring with each other. Each person seems to be fighting against the others with no clear winner or leader. The chaos represents disorganized energy and unfocused competition. Yet no one appears injured — suggesting the conflict is more of a competition than a true battle.

cards.name: Six of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Six of Wands represents public recognition, success, and triumph. Your hard work has paid off and you are being celebrated for your achievements. This is a time of confidence and pride. You have overcome challenges and others are taking notice. Accept the recognition graciously and let it fuel your continued growth.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Six of Wands reversed suggests a fall from grace, lack of recognition, or egotism. Success may be delayed or denied. You may feel overlooked despite your efforts. Alternatively, success may have gone to your head, resulting in arrogance or conceit. There may be private victories that have not yet been publicly recognized.
cards.symbolism: A rider on a white horse is adorned with a laurel wreath and holds a wand also topped with a laurel wreath. He is surrounded by a crowd of supporters waving their own wands in celebration. The white horse represents purity and the triumph of the human spirit.

cards.name: Seven of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Seven of Wands represents standing your ground against opposition and persevering in the face of challenge. You may be under attack or facing stiff competition, but you have the advantage of higher ground. This card calls you to be courageous and defend your position. Do not back down from your convictions.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Seven of Wands reversed suggests giving up, exhaustion from constant battle, and feeling overwhelmed by opposition. You may be conceding defeat unnecessarily or feeling too worn down to fight. There is a sense of defensiveness and anxiety. Consider whether the battle is worth fighting or whether it is time to find a new approach.
cards.symbolism: A man stands on an elevated position, defending himself against six wands poking up from below. He appears to be under attack but holds the high ground. His footing seems unsure — he wears mismatched shoes — suggesting he was caught off guard but is still fighting back. He grips his wand with determination.

cards.name: Eight of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Eight of Wands represents swift movement, rapid progress, and a flurry of activity. After a period of stagnation, things are now moving at an exciting pace. Communication is flowing freely. Travel may be on the horizon. This is a time of dynamic action and rapid change. Everything is moving in the right direction simultaneously.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Eight of Wands reversed suggests delays, frustration, and things coming to a grinding halt. Plans may be stalled or communication may be breaking down. There could be a sense of being stuck after expecting rapid movement. It may also indicate poor timing or resisting the natural flow of events.
cards.symbolism: Eight wands fly through the air in a dynamic diagonal formation over a lush green landscape with a river below. The wands are airborne and moving swiftly toward their destination. There are no people in the image — only the motion and trajectory of the wands, representing pure momentum and direction.

cards.name: Nine of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Nine of Wands represents resilience and the courage to persist even when exhausted. You have been through the battles and you are nearly at the finish line. This card calls you to dig deep and find the last reserves of strength. You have more than you think. Don't give up when you are so close to victory.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Nine of Wands reversed suggests stubbornness, defensiveness, and an inability to persevere. You may be giving up just before the breakthrough or being overly defensive and paranoid. Alternatively, you may be persisting in something that is no longer worth the effort. Reassess and decide whether to continue or redirect your energy.
cards.symbolism: A weary, bandaged man leans on a wand, looking back over his shoulder with a guarded expression. Eight wands are planted firmly behind him in a row, forming a defensive barrier. Despite his wounds, he stands firm and ready for the next challenge. His posture is defensive but not defeated.

cards.name: Ten of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Ten of Wands represents carrying a heavy burden and being overwhelmed by responsibilities. You may have taken on more than you can handle. The end is in sight but the load is heavy. This card asks you to consider what you can delegate or release. You are nearly at your destination — do not let the weight break you before you arrive.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Ten of Wands reversed suggests releasing burdens, delegating, and finding relief from oppressive responsibilities. You may be learning to let go of what is no longer yours to carry. Alternatively, it can indicate that you are collapsing under the weight of responsibilities or trying to do everything alone when help is available.
cards.symbolism: A figure struggles to carry ten heavy wands toward a small town in the distance. He is bent under the weight and can barely see where he is going. The town represents the goal — almost in reach. The burdens he carries are of his own choosing, suggesting the weight is self-imposed.

cards.name: Page of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Page of Wands represents a free spirit full of creative energy, enthusiasm, and the desire for adventure. This card often signals the arrival of exciting news or a new creative opportunity. Approach life with curiosity and openness. You may be in the early stages of discovering your passion or developing a new skill.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Page of Wands reversed suggests a lack of direction, scattered energy, and unfulfilled potential. Creative energy is there but it is not being focused. There may be many ideas but no follow-through. Watch out for becoming distracted, overly ambitious without action, or engaging in petty gossip.
cards.symbolism: A young man stands in a desert landscape, holding a wand that is taller than himself. He wears a tunic decorated with salamanders — a symbol of fire. He gazes at the wand with wonder and curiosity, as if it is a magical object. The pyramids in the background represent ancient mystery and potential.

cards.name: Knight of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Knight of Wands represents a burst of passionate, adventurous energy and a desire for action. He is charismatic, daring, and always up for a challenge. This card encourages you to pursue your goals with confidence and energy. Be bold and take action, but be careful not to act so impulsively that you burn out or create chaos.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Knight of Wands reversed warns of recklessness, impulsiveness, and restlessness. Energy may be scattered or misdirected. There is a tendency to start things without finishing them. Be wary of acting without thinking or making decisions based purely on excitement. Harness the energy more mindfully.
cards.symbolism: A knight on a fiery, rearing horse charges forward with a wand raised high. He wears a yellow tunic adorned with salamanders and a helmet with a plume of fire. The desert behind him represents the wild, untamed quality of fire energy. His horse rears up, suggesting barely contained energy.

cards.name: Queen of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The Queen of Wands represents a vibrant, confident, and independent woman who commands respect. She is passionate, courageous, and deeply connected to her desires. This card encourages you to be bold, to own your power, and to approach life with warmth and determination. You have the ability to inspire and attract others through your natural charisma.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Queen of Wands reversed suggests jealousy, insecurity, and a demanding nature. There may be a tendency toward selfishness or an inability to focus your fiery energy productively. You or someone around you may be using their charisma manipulatively. Reconnect with your authentic passion rather than performing for others.
cards.symbolism: The Queen sits on a throne decorated with lions and sunflowers. She holds a sunflower in one hand and a wand in the other. A black cat sits at her feet, representing intuition and mystery. Sunflowers symbolize joy, fertility, and satisfaction. Lions represent fire and strength. She embodies confident feminine fire energy.

cards.name: King of Wands
cards.upright_meaning: The King of Wands represents a bold, visionary leader who inspires others through his passion and big-picture thinking. He is an entrepreneur and innovator, always on the lookout for the next great venture. This card calls you to lead with vision and passion, to think boldly, and to inspire those around you with your enthusiasm and confidence.
cards.reversed_meaning: The King of Wands reversed suggests an overbearing, impulsive leader who is high on vision but low on follow-through. There may be a tendency toward arrogance, ruthlessness, or setting unrealistic expectations. Alternatively, this energy may be lacking — a vision without the courage to pursue it.
cards.symbolism: The King sits on a throne decorated with lions and salamanders. He wears a crown and cloak decorated with the same salamanders as the rest of the Wands court, representing fire. A live lizard sits at his feet. He holds his wand loosely, suggesting that his power is natural and confident rather than forced.

cards.name: Ace of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Ace of Cups represents the beginning of a new emotional journey, overflowing with love, compassion, and joy. Your heart is open and ready to give and receive love. This is a time of emotional abundance and spiritual renewal. New relationships, creative endeavors, or spiritual experiences may be beginning. The cup of life is overflowing.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Ace of Cups reversed suggests emotional blockages, a closed heart, and suppressed feelings. You may be struggling to open up emotionally or to receive love. There may be a creative block or spiritual disconnection. It is time to release what is keeping your heart closed and allow yourself to feel again.
cards.symbolism: A hand emerges from a cloud offering a cup overflowing with five streams of water. A dove descends bearing a communion wafer. The water represents the subconscious and the emotional realm. The dove represents peace and divine love. Lotus blossoms float on the water below, representing spiritual enlightenment.

cards.name: Two of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Two of Cups represents a deep, harmonious connection between two people. This may be a romantic partnership, friendship, or business alliance. There is a profound mutual attraction and a sense of equality and respect. This card celebrates the magic of genuine connection and the power of unity. A new relationship may be beginning.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Two of Cups reversed suggests broken partnerships, imbalance in relationships, and disconnection. A relationship may be falling apart or losing its harmony. There may be a lack of reciprocity or respect. It can also indicate self-love issues — an inability to love oneself before loving others.
cards.symbolism: A man and woman face each other, exchanging cups in a ritual gesture. Between them rises a caduceus — a staff with two intertwined serpents topped by a lion's head with wings. The caduceus represents commerce and negotiation; the lion and wings represent passion and fire. They stand in a lush garden, representing abundance.

cards.name: Three of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Three of Cups represents celebration, friendship, and the joy of community. This is a time to gather with those you love and celebrate shared accomplishments. Creative collaborations are especially fruitful now. Reunions, parties, and group activities bring happiness. Lean on your support network and allow others to celebrate you.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Three of Cups reversed warns of overindulgence, gossip, and superficial social connections. You may be partying too much or engaging in meaningless social activities. There may be a third wheel in a relationship causing tension. Friendships may be turning sour or feeling superficial. Focus on quality rather than quantity in your social life.
cards.symbolism: Three women dance in a circle, each raising a cup in joyful celebration. The ground around them is covered with fruits and flowers, representing abundance and harvest. They celebrate together in a spirit of complete joy and sisterhood. The image radiates warmth, community, and shared happiness.

cards.name: Four of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Four of Cups represents a period of introspection, apathy, or dissatisfaction with what life currently offers. You may be so caught up in your own inner world that you are missing opportunities being presented to you. This card invites you to look up and take stock of what is being offered. Your discontentment may be pointing you toward a necessary change.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Four of Cups reversed suggests emerging from withdrawal, renewed motivation, and seizing missed opportunities. You are ready to re-engage with life after a period of introspection. You may have a new perspective that allows you to appreciate what was previously being overlooked. It can also indicate excessive retreat from the world.
cards.symbolism: A young man sits with his arms crossed under a tree, contemplating three cups before him. A divine hand extends from a cloud offering him a fourth cup, which he ignores. The landscape is peaceful and green. His closed-off body language suggests he is turned inward, unable to see the gift being offered.

cards.name: Five of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Five of Cups represents grief, loss, and the pain of regret. Three cups have spilled and you are focused on what has been lost. However, two cups still stand behind you, representing what remains. This card invites you to allow yourself to grieve but also to turn around and see what has not been lost. Not everything is gone.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Five of Cups reversed suggests recovery from grief, acceptance, and moving on. You are beginning to pick yourself up after a loss and finding hope again. You may be reaching a place of forgiveness or acceptance. Alternatively, you may be suppressing your grief rather than processing it, which can delay healing.
cards.symbolism: A cloaked figure stands in mourning before three spilled cups, not noticing the two upright cups behind him. A bridge in the background leads to a castle, representing the path forward that he is not yet able to see. The river running through the scene represents the flow of emotion.

cards.name: Six of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Six of Cups represents nostalgia, happy memories, and reconnecting with your past. You may be revisiting childhood memories or reuniting with someone from your past. There is an innocence and purity to this card that speaks to simple joys. Sharing and giving freely to others brings fulfillment. Playfulness and creative expression are highlighted.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Six of Cups reversed suggests living in the past, being unable to move forward, or idealizing the past. You may be stuck in nostalgia or longing for what was. It is time to release the past and fully inhabit the present. Alternatively, this can indicate a return of a past lover or unresolved issues from childhood surfacing.
cards.symbolism: A young boy hands a cup filled with flowers to a little girl. Five other cups also overflow with white flowers. They stand in a courtyard of a large house, evoking a sense of security and warmth. The flowers represent gifts of love and memory. The scene has a timeless, fairy-tale quality that evokes the innocence of childhood.

cards.name: Seven of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Seven of Cups represents a wealth of options, fantasies, and illusions. You may be in a dream-like state with many choices before you, not all of which are what they seem. This card warns against wishful thinking and escapism. Clarity and discernment are needed. Not all that glitters is gold — examine your options carefully before committing.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Seven of Cups reversed suggests clarity emerging from confusion, making a firm decision, or recognizing an illusion for what it is. You are cutting through the fantasy and seeing reality more clearly. You may have recently woken up from a delusion or made a firm decision after a period of indecision.
cards.symbolism: A figure stands in shadow before seven cups floating in clouds. Each cup contains a different vision: a castle, jewels, a wreath of laurels, a figure shrouded in light, a dragon, a snake, and a human head. The cups represent dreams and desires, but the clouds suggest they may be illusions or unattainable fantasies.

cards.name: Eight of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Eight of Cups represents walking away from something that no longer fulfills you in search of something more meaningful. Despite achieving what you set out for, there is a sense of emotional dissatisfaction. You are being called to leave behind the familiar and journey toward greater spiritual fulfillment, even if the path is uncertain.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Eight of Cups reversed suggests staying in an unfulfilling situation out of fear, aimless drifting, or confusion about direction. You may be too afraid to walk away from something that has run its course. Alternatively, you may be drifting without purpose or running away from problems rather than facing them.
cards.symbolism: A figure walks away at night toward steep mountains, leaving behind eight cups neatly stacked in the foreground. The moon partially eclipses the sun, casting an eerie light. The cups are all present and accounted for but something is missing — there is a gap in the arrangement. The journey ahead is difficult but necessary.

cards.name: Nine of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Nine of Cups is the 'wish card' — a sign that your heart's desires are coming to fruition. This is a time of deep contentment, satisfaction, and emotional fulfillment. You have much to be grateful for. Enjoy the pleasures of life and celebrate your blessings. Your wishes are being granted by the universe.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Nine of Cups reversed warns of overindulgence, greed, and wish fulfillment at others' expense. You may have gotten what you wished for but find it is not what you expected. There may be an obsession with material pleasures or a sense of smugness. Look beyond surface-level satisfaction to deeper sources of fulfillment.
cards.symbolism: A well-dressed, satisfied man sits with his arms crossed and a smile on his face. Behind him nine cups are arranged in a curved row on a shelf, like trophies. His posture radiates contentment and self-satisfaction. The blue cloth behind the cups represents the emotional realm fully satisfied and in order.

cards.name: Ten of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Ten of Cups represents the highest form of emotional fulfillment — a happy family, harmonious relationships, and divine love. This is a card of lasting joy and peace. Your emotional world is in perfect alignment. This card often signals a deeply satisfying domestic life or the culmination of an emotional journey into lasting happiness.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Ten of Cups reversed suggests dysfunctional family dynamics, broken relationships, and an elusive sense of happiness. The happy home you dream of feels out of reach. There may be conflict within your family or close relationships. Alternatively, you may be sacrificing your own emotional needs for the sake of keeping the peace.
cards.symbolism: Two adults stand with arms raised joyfully, watching two children dance in a field. Above them, a rainbow arc holds ten cups. A beautiful home and rolling hills are in the background. The image represents an idealized vision of domestic happiness and emotional harmony — the feeling that all is right with the world.

cards.name: Page of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Page of Cups represents a sensitive, creative, and intuitive young energy. This card often brings an unexpected or unusual message — perhaps a creative opportunity or an invitation to explore your emotional world. Be open to the unexpected. This Page follows his heart over his head and is deeply in touch with his feelings and imagination.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Page of Cups reversed suggests emotional immaturity, creative blocks, and escapism. There may be a tendency to use fantasy as an escape from reality. Emotional messages or creative opportunities may be blocked or misunderstood. An overly sensitive or petty person may be causing difficulties.
cards.symbolism: A young man stands at the seashore holding a cup from which a fish unexpectedly pops out. He looks at the fish with surprised delight. His blue tunic is decorated with flowers. The fish represents a message from the unconscious — an unexpected creative or intuitive insight rising to the surface.

cards.name: Knight of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Knight of Cups is the romantic idealist — the poet, the artist, and the dreamer. He arrives as a messenger bringing an invitation, proposal, or creative offer. He follows his heart wherever it leads. This card encourages you to follow your heart and pursue your dreams with romantic passion. An important offer may be on the way.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Knight of Cups reversed warns of moodiness, unrealistic fantasies, and manipulation. The romantic idealism has curdled into deception or disappointment. Someone may be all talk with no follow-through. You may be pursuing fantasies that bear no fruit. Ground your dreams in reality before taking action.
cards.symbolism: A knight rides calmly on a white horse, holding a cup aloft. Unlike the other knights, he moves slowly and peacefully, reflecting the calm of water over the passion of fire. He wears winged helmet and boots, representing an active imagination. Fish adorn his tunic, representing the watery realm of emotions.

cards.name: Queen of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The Queen of Cups represents deep emotional intelligence, compassion, and intuitive wisdom. She is deeply empathic and attuned to the emotional needs of those around her. This card encourages you to lead with your heart, to trust your intuition, and to offer others the gift of your emotional presence. True healing and connection come through vulnerability.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Queen of Cups reversed suggests emotional insecurity, codependency, and being overwhelmed by emotion. You may be absorbing others' emotions to your own detriment or struggling with your own emotional volatility. There is a need to establish healthy emotional boundaries and reconnect with your own inner stability.
cards.symbolism: The Queen sits on a throne at the edge of the sea. She holds an ornate, closed cup — suggesting that her insights come from within, from her own subconscious. The throne is decorated with mermaids and water nymphs. She is surrounded by water, representing emotional depth and intuitive knowledge.

cards.name: King of Cups
cards.upright_meaning: The King of Cups represents emotional maturity, compassion, and the mastery of balancing emotions with intellect. He rules his emotional realm with wisdom and grace. This card encourages you to lead with both your heart and your head — to remain calm and centered even in emotionally charged situations. He is the master of diplomacy and emotional intelligence.
cards.reversed_meaning: The King of Cups reversed suggests emotional manipulation, moodiness, and a man who uses emotional intelligence for personal gain. Someone may be using emotional tactics to control or manipulate. You may be struggling with emotional volatility or escapism. Reclaim your emotional center and lead from a place of genuine compassion.
cards.symbolism: The King sits on a throne floating in turbulent seas, yet he remains calm and unshaken. He holds a cup and a scepter. A fish amulet hangs from his neck. Despite the churning waters around him, he is at peace — representing the ability to remain emotionally stable and centered even in turbulent circumstances.

cards.name: Ace of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Ace of Swords represents a breakthrough in thinking, mental clarity, and the power of truth. A new idea or insight has cut through confusion like a blade. This is a time of intellectual power and clear communication. Truth will prevail. You have the mental fortitude to overcome any obstacle. Speak and act with integrity.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Ace of Swords reversed suggests confusion, chaos, and a lack of mental clarity. You may be struggling to think clearly or communicate effectively. A new idea may not be as solid as it first appeared. Misinformation or unclear thinking is causing problems. Cut through the noise and seek the truth.
cards.symbolism: A hand emerges from a cloud holding a sword upright, crowned with a wreath and a crown. The sword represents the power of the mind and truth. Yods (divine sparks) fall around it. Jagged mountains in the background represent the difficult terrain of the intellect. The crown at the top represents achievement through mental mastery.

cards.name: Two of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Two of Swords represents a stalemate, indecision, and an avoidance of the truth. You may be refusing to look at a situation clearly, keeping yourself blindfolded to avoid making a difficult choice. A truce may have been reached but underlying tensions remain. The time has come to remove the blindfold and face the truth, however uncomfortable.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Two of Swords reversed suggests that the stalemate is breaking down, a difficult truth is emerging, or a decision can no longer be avoided. Information that was hidden is coming to light. You are ready to remove the blindfold and face what needs to be faced. However, it can also indicate information overload and an inability to choose.
cards.symbolism: A blindfolded woman sits before a crescent moon, holding two crossed swords on her chest. The blindfold represents willful ignorance. The crossed swords represent the mental impasse she is in. The crescent moon represents the subconscious knowledge she is suppressing. The sea behind her represents the emotional world she is shutting out.

cards.name: Three of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Three of Swords represents heartbreak, sorrow, and emotional pain. Three swords pierce a heart, leaving no ambiguity about the nature of this pain. You may be experiencing grief, betrayal, or a loss that cuts to the core. Allow yourself to feel the pain — it is a necessary part of healing. This too shall pass.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Three of Swords reversed suggests recovery from grief, releasing pain, and forgiveness. The worst of the heartbreak is over and healing is beginning. You may be ready to forgive and move on. Alternatively, old wounds may be reopening that need to be properly healed. Suppressing grief only prolongs the pain.
cards.symbolism: Three swords pierce a red heart against a backdrop of stormy, rain-filled clouds. The image is brutally direct — there is no ambiguity here. The heart represents the emotional self. The three swords represent the precise nature of the pain — a specific wound with a specific cause. The storm represents the turbulent emotional climate.

cards.name: Four of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Four of Swords represents a necessary period of rest, retreat, and recuperation. After a period of intense activity or conflict, your mind and body need time to recover. This is not a time for action but for rest, contemplation, and inner preparation. Take this time to recharge so you can re-enter the world refreshed.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Four of Swords reversed suggests restlessness, burnout from overactivity, and a refusal to rest. You may be pushing yourself too hard without allowing adequate recovery time. Alternatively, it can indicate that a period of rest is coming to an end and it is time to re-enter the world and engage with life again.
cards.symbolism: A knight or noble lies in repose on a tomb in a church. His hands are folded in prayer. Three swords hang on the wall above him; one lies along his body. A stained glass window above shows a figure in prayer. The tomb represents temporary withdrawal from the world. The church represents sanctuary and peace.

cards.name: Five of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Five of Swords represents conflict, defeat, and winning at all costs. Someone has won a battle but at what price? A conflict may have ended with a hollow victory — winning but losing respect, integrity, or relationships in the process. This card warns against the pursuit of victory through dishonest or dishonorable means.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Five of Swords reversed suggests moving past conflict, reconciliation, and releasing resentment. A conflict is coming to an end and forgiveness is possible. Alternatively, it can indicate an unresolved conflict that continues to fester, or a pattern of conflict and drama that you seem unable to escape.
cards.symbolism: A smirking figure holds three swords while two more lie on the ground. Two defeated figures walk away in the background, their heads bowed. The stormy sky reflects the turbulent nature of the conflict. The winner's smug expression suggests a hollow victory — he has won, but at the cost of his relationships and honor.

cards.name: Six of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Six of Swords represents a transition from turbulence to calmer waters. You are moving away from difficulty and toward greater peace, even if the journey is still challenging. This is a card of necessary change and gradual healing. You may be physically or emotionally traveling away from a difficult situation toward something better.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Six of Swords reversed suggests resistance to transition, inability to move on, and carrying too much baggage. You may be unable to leave a difficult situation or reluctant to make a necessary change. The journey is stalled. You may also be returning to a past situation that you thought you had left behind.
cards.symbolism: A ferryman poles a small boat across water, carrying a woman and child. Six swords are stuck upright in the bow of the boat. The water on the right side is choppy; on the left it is calm — they are traveling from turbulence to peace. The passengers look downcast, suggesting this move was not chosen lightly.

cards.name: Seven of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Seven of Swords represents deception, betrayal, and someone acting in a sneaky or underhanded manner. Someone may be getting away with something, or you may need to use strategy and stealth to navigate a difficult situation. This card warns you to watch your back and be alert to deception. Not everything is as it appears.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Seven of Swords reversed suggests coming clean, being caught, and the uncovering of deception. A secret is being revealed or a deception is coming to light. Someone who was getting away with something is about to be caught. It can also suggest a desire to unburden yourself of guilt through confession.
cards.symbolism: A figure tiptoes away from a military camp, carrying five swords. He looks back over his shoulder with a sly expression. Two swords are left behind. The tents of the camp are in the background. His furtive expression and posture suggest he is stealing away with what is not rightfully his.

cards.name: Eight of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Eight of Swords represents a sense of being trapped, restricted, and unable to move forward. However, the prison is largely of your own making — created by negative thinking, limiting beliefs, and self-victimization. You have more freedom than you think. Remove the blindfold of fear and you will see a way out. The chains are loose.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Eight of Swords reversed suggests releasing limiting beliefs, regaining freedom, and taking back personal power. You are beginning to see that your prison was self-imposed. The blindfold is coming off. However, it can also indicate an intensification of feeling trapped, or a refusal to acknowledge the role you play in your own captivity.
cards.symbolism: A blindfolded woman stands with her arms bound and eight swords planted around her in a circle. Though she appears trapped, the binding is loose and the swords do not actually form a complete cage — she could walk away if she could see. The castle in the background represents the safety she thinks she is shut out from.

cards.name: Nine of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Nine of Swords represents anxiety, worry, and the dark night of the soul. This is a card of mental anguish — the kind that wakes you at 3am and fills your mind with worst-case scenarios. The suffering is real but often greater in the mind than in reality. Seek support, speak your fears aloud, and reach out for help.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Nine of Swords reversed suggests the worst is over, moving through darkness, or suppressing deep anxiety. You may be beginning to emerge from a period of despair, or you may be internalizing suffering that needs to be released. Seeking help — whether from others or professional support — is especially important now.
cards.symbolism: A figure sits bolt upright in bed, head in hands, in obvious despair. Nine swords hang horizontally on the dark wall above. The quilt is covered with roses and astrological symbols. Despite the bleakness of the scene, the quilt suggests that beauty and order exist — even in the darkest moments.

cards.name: Ten of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Ten of Swords represents a painful ending, betrayal, and hitting rock bottom. Something has come to a brutal and final end. Though the pain is intense, this card also carries a message of hope — you cannot fall lower than this. The dawn is beginning to break on the horizon. A new chapter must now begin.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Ten of Swords reversed suggests recovery from a painful ending, learning from loss, and finding a way to rise again. The crisis has passed or is lessening in intensity. You are beginning to gather yourself after a difficult fall. It can also indicate resistance to accepting a necessary and painful ending.
cards.symbolism: A figure lies face down with ten swords stabbed into his back. One hand is turned palm up in a gesture of surrender. Despite the brutal scene, the sky shows calm water, the horizon is glowing with the light of dawn, and in the distance the sun begins to rise. The darkest moment is also the dawn of something new.

cards.name: Page of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Page of Swords represents a curious, quick-minded energy eager to learn and to speak the truth. News or information may be arriving. This Page is alert, vigilant, and always ready to defend what is right. Approach situations with curiosity and an open mind. There is a youthful mental energy here that thrives on new ideas.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Page of Swords reversed warns of gossip, deception, and all talk with no action. This energy has turned sharp-tongued and cruel, using intellect as a weapon. There may be rumors spreading or someone being two-faced. It can also indicate scattered thinking and an inability to focus mental energy productively.
cards.symbolism: A young man stands on a hilltop with a sword raised, poised and alert. The wind tosses his hair and the clouds swirl behind him. Though he holds his sword defensively, he looks out with curiosity rather than aggression. Birds fly overhead. His posture suggests readiness and vigilance rather than aggression.

cards.name: Knight of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Knight of Swords is fast, direct, and driven by logic and intellect. He charges forward with total conviction, cutting through obstacles with his sharp mind. This card encourages you to be assertive and action-oriented in pursuit of your goals. However, be sure to think before you act — the Knight's haste can sometimes create more problems than it solves.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Knight of Swords reversed suggests aggression, recklessness, and rushing headlong into situations without thinking. There is a destructive, impulsive energy here that creates chaos. Alternatively, it can indicate intellectual paralysis — the inability to act even with all the information at hand.
cards.symbolism: A knight charges on a white horse at full gallop, sword raised. His horse's mane and the trees around him are bent by the fierce wind he creates. His expression is intense and focused. He wears armor to protect himself in his single-minded charge. The stormy clouds behind him suggest the chaos that often follows such recklessness.

cards.name: Queen of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The Queen of Swords is sharp, clear-minded, and independent. She has learned through experience — often painful — and now sees the world with clarity and wisdom. She cuts through nonsense and communicates with precision. This card encourages clear, honest communication and the setting of firm boundaries. Let your experience be your guide.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Queen of Swords reversed suggests coldness, cruelty, and using one's intelligence to wound others. Words may be cutting and unkind. There may be a tendency toward bitterness based on past hurts. Alternatively, this energy may be turned inward as harsh self-criticism. Soften the blade of the intellect with compassion.
cards.symbolism: The Queen sits upright on her throne with one hand raised in greeting and one holding a sword upright. She faces forward, directly and without evasion. Her crown is adorned with butterflies and angels. A single bird flies in the stormy sky. Her severe expression reflects clear judgment unclouded by sentiment.

cards.name: King of Swords
cards.upright_meaning: The King of Swords is the master of intellect, truth, and ethical authority. He leads with his mind and demands the same clarity of thought from those around him. He represents a fair but demanding judge, mentor, or authority figure. This card calls you to think clearly, speak honestly, and lead with integrity. The truth must guide all decisions.
cards.reversed_meaning: The King of Swords reversed suggests tyranny, abuse of power, and the use of intellect for manipulation and control. An authority figure may be using logic and power in unjust ways. Alternatively, your own mental faculties may be working against you — overthinking, cold detachment, or ruthless criticism.
cards.symbolism: The King sits upright on a throne, sword held straight up. His gaze is forward and direct. Two birds fly in the blue sky. Unlike the chaotic scenes of many Swords cards, his throne and sky are relatively clear — he has mastered the turbulent energy of his suit. Butterflies on his throne represent transformation through thought.

cards.name: Ace of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Ace of Pentacles represents a new financial or material opportunity. A seed of prosperity is being offered to you. This may come as a new job, business venture, or financial windfall. Seize this opportunity with both hands — the potential for material success and stability is great. Plant this seed wisely and tend to it carefully.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Ace of Pentacles reversed suggests a missed opportunity, poor financial planning, and greed. The opportunity for material growth has been squandered or has not yet materialized. You may be focusing too much on money at the expense of other areas of life, or failing to recognize a valuable opportunity when it appears.
cards.symbolism: A hand extends from a cloud, offering a large golden pentacle. Below is a beautiful garden with an archway of flowers leading to mountains in the distance. The garden represents cultivated abundance. The path through the arch represents the journey toward financial and material success that this opportunity opens up.

cards.name: Two of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Two of Pentacles represents the act of juggling multiple priorities and managing resources with skill and adaptability. You are balancing different aspects of your life — work, finances, relationships — and managing to keep all the balls in the air. This is a dynamic equilibrium rather than a stable one. Stay flexible and keep adapting.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Two of Pentacles reversed suggests overwhelm, imbalance, and an inability to manage competing demands. You may be dropping balls — important areas of your life are suffering due to poor time management or over-commitment. It is time to simplify, prioritize, and ask for help if needed.
cards.symbolism: A young man juggles two pentacles connected by an infinity symbol. Ships sail on rough seas in the background, representing the ups and downs of life. The infinity symbol represents the perpetual nature of balance — it is never fixed but always in motion. His dance-like posture suggests ease and adaptability.

cards.name: Three of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Three of Pentacles represents collaboration, skilled work, and the early stages of a building project. Your skills are being recognized and valued. Working with a team produces better results than working alone. This is a time to combine your talents with others and create something of lasting value. Master your craft.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Three of Pentacles reversed suggests poor teamwork, a lack of skill, and a disregard for others' input. Projects are suffering because people are not working well together. There may be ego conflicts or a refusal to collaborate. Alternatively, someone may be failing to listen to expert advice.
cards.symbolism: A sculptor works on a cathedral, consulting with a monk and a nobleman who hold the architectural plans. The three figures represent a team working together — each contributing something different to the shared vision. The cathedral represents a grand project that requires sustained skill, collaboration, and commitment.

cards.name: Four of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Four of Pentacles represents holding on tightly to what you have — security, stability, and the need for control. You may be saving and conserving resources wisely, or you may be hoarding and resisting the natural flow of abundance. Stability is important but not at the cost of generosity and openness to change.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Four of Pentacles reversed suggests releasing control, generosity, and overcoming a scarcity mindset. You may be letting go of material concerns, becoming more generous, or releasing a need to control outcomes. Alternatively, financial instability may be causing anxiety and a need to hold on tighter.
cards.symbolism: A crowned figure sits with a pentacle balanced on his head, clutching one to his chest, and placing his feet on two others. He turns his back on his city, hoarding his wealth. His posture is defensive and closed. The pentacles he clings to represent both his security and his inability to grow beyond what he already has.

cards.name: Five of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Five of Pentacles represents a time of financial difficulty, hardship, and feeling left out in the cold. You may be experiencing a material or spiritual poverty. However, help is available — the lit church window above the struggling figures suggests refuge is near. This card asks you to seek help and to have faith that this difficult period will pass.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Five of Pentacles reversed suggests recovery from financial hardship, improved circumstances, and an end to isolation. Things are looking up after a difficult period. You may be finding new sources of support, financial relief, or spiritual renewal. The worst is over.
cards.symbolism: Two figures trudge through the snow past a church with a stained glass window showing five pentacles. One figure is on crutches, the other is barefoot and in rags. The church represents spiritual warmth and refuge that they seem unaware of or unable to access. Their hardship is both material and spiritual.

cards.name: Six of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Six of Pentacles represents generosity, charity, and the flow of wealth between those who have and those who need. You may be in a position to give or to receive financial support. This card speaks to the importance of balance in financial relationships — giving and receiving with grace and gratitude. Generosity creates a positive cycle of abundance.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Six of Pentacles reversed suggests strings attached to gifts, charity given with judgment, and an imbalance of financial power. Someone may be giving or lending money while using it as a tool of control. There may be an exploitation of power dynamics in financial relationships. Examine the true cost of what is being offered.
cards.symbolism: A wealthy merchant weighs coins on a scale while two beggars kneel before him. He distributes coins to them from his free hand. The scale represents fairness and balance. However, the power dynamic is clear — the rich man stands while the poor men kneel, suggesting that financial charity often comes with an imbalance of power.

cards.name: Seven of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Seven of Pentacles represents a pause to assess your progress and determine whether your investments of time, energy, and resources are yielding the results you desire. You have worked hard and growth is happening, but slowly. This card asks you to be patient and to ensure that your efforts are aligned with your long-term goals.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Seven of Pentacles reversed suggests impatience, poor investment, and a lack of long-term vision. You may be giving up just as things are about to pay off, or you may be pouring energy into something that will never bear fruit. Reassess your investments and make sure your efforts are truly aligned with what you want.
cards.symbolism: A figure rests on his hoe, gazing contemplatively at seven pentacles growing on a large plant. He has been tending this garden with great effort and the results are visible — but the harvest is not yet ready. His posture reflects thoughtful evaluation rather than impatience. He is considering his next move.

cards.name: Eight of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Eight of Pentacles represents dedication to mastering a skill through hard work and repetition. You are putting in the hours required to become truly excellent at your craft. This is a time of focused effort and the joy of growing competence. Diligence and attention to detail will be rewarded. Commit fully to the process of mastery.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Eight of Pentacles reversed suggests perfectionism, lack of ambition, and cutting corners. You may be so focused on getting every detail right that you are unable to complete anything. Alternatively, you may be going through the motions without genuine commitment to improving your skills. Reconnect with the joy of craft.
cards.symbolism: A craftsman sits at his workbench, focused entirely on carving pentacles. Completed pentacles hang in a row beside him and more are arranged in front. He is absorbed in his work, with the town visible in the background — he has set aside social life to focus on his craft. Each pentacle is identical, representing mastery through repetition.

cards.name: Nine of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Nine of Pentacles represents hard-earned abundance, self-sufficiency, and the ability to enjoy the fruits of your labor. You have achieved a level of financial and material independence through your own efforts. This is a time to enjoy luxury, beauty, and the rewards of your sustained effort. You deserve this comfort and security.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Nine of Pentacles reversed warns of financial setbacks, working too hard, and neglecting to enjoy what you have worked for. There may be a superficial pursuit of wealth or success at the cost of genuine fulfillment. Alternatively, you may be overly dependent on others for financial security rather than cultivating your own independence.
cards.symbolism: An elegantly dressed woman stands in a lush vineyard surrounded by nine pentacles. A hooded falcon rests on her gloved hand, representing the mastery of instinct and intellect. A snail moves slowly at her feet, representing patience. She is the embodiment of refinement, abundance, and self-sufficiency achieved through patience and hard work.

cards.name: Ten of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Ten of Pentacles represents lasting wealth, legacy, and multi-generational success. This is the ultimate card of financial security and family stability. You have built something that will endure beyond your own lifetime. This card speaks to the satisfaction of creating a lasting legacy — financially, in your family, or through your work.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Ten of Pentacles reversed warns of family conflict over money or property, financial instability, and the failure of a legacy. What has been built may not endure. There may be disputes within a family over inheritance or values. The long-term stability you hoped for is under threat.
cards.symbolism: An elder sits surrounded by a family: a man and woman discuss while a child plays with two dogs at their feet. Ten pentacles are arranged in the pattern of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, representing the perfection of the material world. An archway frames the scene, suggesting that this abundance is firmly established and enduring.

cards.name: Page of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Page of Pentacles represents a studious, practical, and grounded young energy. This Page is eager to learn and to develop new skills, particularly in the material realm. A new financial opportunity or practical project may be beginning. Approach it with curiosity, diligence, and the willingness to put in the work required to succeed.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Page of Pentacles reversed suggests a lack of focus, procrastination, and poor financial planning. You may have the potential but are not applying yourself. There is a tendency toward laziness or immaturity in practical matters. It is time to buckle down and commit to the work required to achieve your goals.
cards.symbolism: A young man stands in a beautiful landscape, gazing intently at the pentacle he holds before him. He is absorbed in contemplation of it, as if studying its properties. The fertile landscape around him — green fields, mountains, trees — represents the potential for material growth that awaits those who apply themselves with focus.

cards.name: Knight of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Knight of Pentacles is methodical, hardworking, and deeply reliable. He does not cut corners or rush. His approach is slow and steady but it always wins the race. This card encourages you to commit to the long process of doing things right. Develop systems, establish routines, and work consistently toward your goals.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Knight of Pentacles reversed suggests becoming stuck in routine, boredom, and a lack of progress. You may be so locked into your methods that you have become inflexible. Alternatively, you may be neglecting your responsibilities or becoming lazy. Find a way to refresh your commitment to the work.
cards.symbolism: Unlike the other knights who charge forward, the Knight of Pentacles sits motionless on his horse in a plowed field. He examines a pentacle with focused attention. His heavy black horse represents patience and endurance. The plowed fields behind him represent the methodical labor he has already performed. He is in no hurry.

cards.name: Queen of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The Queen of Pentacles is a nurturing, practical, and highly capable woman who creates abundance and security for those in her care. She is resourceful, warm, and deeply connected to the physical world. This card encourages you to create a comfortable, nurturing environment for yourself and others. Financial and practical security come through thoughtful management of resources.
cards.reversed_meaning: The Queen of Pentacles reversed suggests financial dependency, neglect of home or family, and smothering. There may be an unhealthy focus on material security at the expense of emotional connection. Alternatively, you may be neglecting practical matters or home responsibilities. Rebalance the material and emotional aspects of your life.
cards.symbolism: The Queen sits on an ornate throne in a beautiful garden, cradling a pentacle in her lap. She gazes at it tenderly, as if it were a child. Flowers and fruit surround her throne. A rabbit — symbolizing abundance and fertility — runs at the corner of the card. She is the embodiment of earthly abundance and maternal generosity.

cards.name: King of Pentacles
cards.upright_meaning: The King of Pentacles is the master of the material world — a self-made, disciplined, and abundantly successful leader who has achieved prosperity through hard work and sound judgment. He is a generous and reliable provider. This card encourages you to pursue material success with discipline and integrity, and to use your resources to benefit others.
cards.reversed_meaning: The King of Pentacles reversed warns of financial corruption, greed, and an obsession with wealth at the expense of everything else. There may be a ruthless or unethical approach to business. Alternatively, you may be financially irresponsible or unable to maintain what you have built. Money has become the master rather than the tool.
cards.symbolism: The King sits on a throne decorated with bulls (representing Taurus) and vines. He wears a robe decorated with grapes and flowers, representing abundance. He holds a scepter and a large pentacle. The castle behind him represents the material empire he has built. He is completely at home in the world of money and material success.

metadata.description: Complete Rider-Waite-Smith tarot deck with upright and reversed meanings, symbolism, keywords, and elemental/astrological associations.
